target_customer: California homeowners seeking energy-efficient upgrades such as heat pumps, and the contractors who quote them
problem: Getting contractor quotes for home upgrades took weeks and site visits; HomeBreeze scoped projects remotely from photos and sent them to contractors for quotes within minutes.
business_model: Marketplace and lead generation taking fees from contractors on upgrade jobs
product_category: Home services marketplace with AI scoping

founders.name: Vineet Mehta
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built HomeBreeze and sold it to the largest US contracting firm; also worked as a VC investor.

founders.name: Christopher Ager
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him with marketplaces and B2B SaaS experience; education not listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Remote project scoping from photos and answers, contractor network management and quoting; image-based scoping was a hard part in 2021 for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: A contractor network and customer reviews (4.97 average) help, but quoting marketplaces could be copied and larger home service players existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Apex Service Partners acquired HomeBreeze on 2024-11-26 per a deal listing, bringing its technology and California customers into Apex.

market_need_then: Heat pump and efficiency upgrades were pushed by California rebates and tax credits; the HomeBreeze site promotes finding rebates, and Sealed raised $16M in June 2021 for the same category.

branding.domain_note: Used homebreeze.ai in later years (YC lists homebreeze.ai as the website).

identity.voice_and_tone: Site stresses speed and ease with free no-obligation scopes

branding.community_and_virality: No press about the brand itself was found; the site shows customer reviews and project photos.

brand_strength.rationale: The name is warm and fits cooling and heating but is generic and shared with several other Breeze companies, which crowded search results; no brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: HomeBreeze served thousands of California customers with remote AI scoping and was acquired by Apex Service Partners in November 2024, which is an exit though the price and any shutdown of the brand are not public. YC marks it inactive because of the acquisition; the sources do not show the total capital raised, so how efficient the path was cannot be judged.
notes: The $130K seed rests on one database (CB Insights, dated 1 Sep 2021) and matches the size of YC's standard deal; VCBacked dates a seed to Aug 2021 and adds Point72 and Liquid 2 Ventures as investors without an amount, a conflict. A team of 45 and 5,000 plus jobs suggest more capital than recorded, so a gap is likely. The acquisition rests on a deal listing dated 2024-11-26 and the YC page; price is not stated. Sealed is cited from a June 2021 article, about five months after the Winter 2021 batch start. Crunchbase lists a Newport Beach location, which conflicts with San Francisco on YC. Correction: the August 2021 round with Point72 and Liquid 2 Ventures rests on a single database (VCBacked) and no amount is given; it may be the same financing as the CB Insights 2021-09 seed. Sealed was removed from competitors because the Axios source (2021-06) is dated after the as_of of 2021-01 and no better dated source was found.
